This is a lesson on one bass line the [Backing Track](../../tools/backing-track.qmd) band plays: **Dotted (1, and of 2, 3)**. It is built up from 2 simpler patterns, one step at a time, and every step is played by the band and written out as it plays. How the examples work: press ▶ Play, switch players in and out with the buttons beside it, and read what the band will play on the staff underneath: the whole pass is written out when Play starts, before it sounds. The tempo slider at the bottom of the page slows everything down.

[All the accompaniment patterns](index.qmd) · [Bass lines](index.qmd#bass)

## The pattern

The root on beat 1, again on the and of 2 and on beat 3, the same rhythm as the kick drum. Every second bar ends with an eighth note that leads into the next chord.

It belongs in *Acoustic strum*, *Piano ballad*, *Straight-eighth rock* and *Emo / pop-punk*. Here it is in the acoustic strum style with the whole band. Switch the other players off to hear it alone.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="strum" data-chart="C|G|Am|F" data-tempo="96" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="bass drums" data-choice-label="Bass line:" data-choices='[{"label":"Dotted (1, and of 2, 3)","opts":{"bassFeel":"dotted"}}]'></div>

## Step 1: Roots on 1 and 3

Start with something simpler. The root on beats 1 and 3, held; one note a bar in 3/4. A chord that changes in between gets its root when it arrives.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](bass-halves.qmd) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="strum" data-chart="C|G|Am|F" data-tempo="68" data-on="bass drums" data-staves="bass" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Roots on 1 and 3","opts":{"bassFeel":"halves"}}]'></div>

## Step 2: Roots on every beat

The root of the chord on every beat and nothing else. The plainest line there is, under driving eighths or a strummed song.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](bass-roots.qmd) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="strum" data-chart="C|G|Am|F" data-tempo="68" data-on="bass drums" data-staves="bass" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Roots on every beat","opts":{"bassFeel":"roots"}}]'></div>

## Step 3: Dotted (1, and of 2, 3), slowly

Now the pattern itself. Compare it with the step before: press each button while the band plays and watch what changes on the staff.

**How to play it.** Say it: ONE (and) two AND three. The note on the and of 2 is the push that makes it pop music. Every second bar, the last eighth note walks into the next root from a step below or above.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="strum" data-chart="C|G|Am|F" data-tempo="68" data-on="bass drums" data-staves="bass" data-choice-label="Compare:" data-choices='[{"label":"Dotted (1, and of 2, 3)","opts":{"bassFeel":"dotted"}},{"label":"Roots on every beat (the step before)","opts":{"bassFeel":"roots"}}]'></div>

## Step 4: Up to tempo, with the band

The whole band, at 96 beats a minute. Play along, then switch the band's bass off and take the part yourself.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="strum" data-chart="C|G|Am|F" data-tempo="96" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="bass drums" data-choice-label="Bass line:" data-choices='[{"label":"Dotted (1, and of 2, 3)","opts":{"bassFeel":"dotted"}}]'></div>

## Step 5: Two chords in a bar

Harder: now some bars have two chords, two beats each. Each chord gets its root when it arrives; the pattern squeezes into the beats it has.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="strum" data-chart="C G|Am F|C G|F G" data-tempo="96" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="bass" data-choice-label="Bass line:" data-choices='[{"label":"Dotted (1, and of 2, 3)","opts":{"bassFeel":"dotted"}}]'></div>

## How it relates to the other patterns

- **Builds on:** [Roots on 1 and 3](bass-halves.qmd), [Roots on every beat](bass-roots.qmd).
- **Leads to:** [3+3+2 (tresillo)](bass-tresillo.qmd), [Motown: root, fifth, octave](bass-motown.qmd), [Tango (habanera)](bass-tango.qmd), [Boogaloo riff](bass-riff.qmd), [Song for My Father: root, fifth, octave](bass-songfather.qmd), [Maiden Voyage: roots on the rhythm](bass-maiden.qmd): the patterns that use this one as a step.
- **The same idea elsewhere in the band:** [Pop backbeat](drums-strum.qmd) (drum groove), [Song for My Father: root, fifth, octave](bass-songfather.qmd) (bass line), [Ballad](drums-ballad.qmd) (drum groove), [Ballad: rocking](chords-ball-rock.qmd) (comping rhythm).
- **Plays with, in acoustic strum:** [Strum: D, D-U, U-D-U](chords-strum-camp.qmd) (comping rhythm), [Pop backbeat](drums-strum.qmd) (drum groove).
- **Other bass lines in the Folk, rock and pop group:** [Roots on every beat](bass-roots.qmd), [Root and fifth](bass-alt.qmd), [Root and fifth on every beat](bass-polka.qmd), [3+3+2 (tresillo)](bass-tresillo.qmd), [Root eighths](bass-eighths.qmd), [Octaves (disco)](bass-octaves.qmd), [Motown: root, fifth, octave](bass-motown.qmd), [12/8 ballad](bass-twelve8.qmd).
